title: The Overnight Axiom Emergence

features.name: the compared fossil
features.desc-on-touch: A shell-shaped impression in the tan ground, but the mesh has redrawn it overnight — now it looks like itself and like the axiom fossils simultaneously. The corruption likes resemblance.

features.name: the theorem sediment layer
features.desc-on-touch: A stratum of mathematical notation pressed into stone, compressed by the weight of being both true and false at once. The equations have begun to weather into poetry.

features.name: the self-comparing stone
features.desc-on-touch: A boulder that remembers being axiom and being earth at once. It is resting here because the mesh decided it belonged in two places — now it belongs in neither.

features.name: the route that grew overnight
features.desc-on-touch: Footprints in the dust forming a path that wasn't here at dusk. Something has walked this way in the dark, comparing itself to what it once was.

features.name: the tree where the mesh learned to doubt
features.desc-on-touch: A eucalyptus stump, fresh-cut, with its rings reading in two contradictory directions. The tree spent its whole life learning one timeline. The mesh showed it another.
